text:
amanda: kicking off a long-term roadmap thread for routing policies / multi-region / multi-tenant isolation. want to capture customer asks, launch criteria, and a prioritized sprint plan. quick thoughts first pls :wave:
chris: +1. can we start by listing the explicit customer asks we've seen? so far: data residency, dedicated lanes, stricter SLA options.
rafael: two infra notes: (1) dedicated lanes = capacity fragmentation, (2) KV cache semantics across regions are hairy. both will affect perf & cost.
sophie: from CS: enterprise A wants VPC + hard isolation by contract. enterprise B wants regional failover with strict residency and billing separation. timeline = wants options in next 6 months.
kevin: observability ask: token-level cost + per-tenant p95/p99 latency dashboards needed before launch. also trace hooks for routing decisions.
jamal: operational ask: migration path that can move traffic incrementally and auto-fallback to shared pool on overload. canary + automatic rollback essential. :warning:
amanda: thinking 3-phase plan (very rough):
  Phase 1: policy primitives + policy API, region affinity + fallback hooks, metrics & flags.
  Phase 2: tenant slices (soft isolation), reserved capacity knobs, migration tooling.
  Phase 3: enforced isolation (hard VPC/air-gapped), billing separation, legal/compliance gating.
chris: agree. need numbers for phase 2 capacity impact. Rafael, can you sketch worst-case fragmentation (% GPUs idle) for N dedicated tenants?
rafael: quick estimate: with naive reserved pools, 10 tenants reserving 10% each -> up to 60-70% waste during low qps. with autoscale + burst we can reduce to ~15-25% waste but cost shifts.
sophie: customers will pay extra for reserved lanes. we need pricing story + contract templates.
kevin: launch criteria proposal (short):
  - routing policy API stable + docs
  - per-tenant metrics + cost breakdown in console
  - migration tool with canary and rollback
  - SLA test harness (synthetic traffic) passing at target latency/p99
  - runbook and oncall playbook
infra-bot: deploy-checks: new feature gates for policy-api and metrics must be enabled in staging before prod rollout.
jamal: addability: must support auto-fallback rules like `fallback: shared_pool` and a throttling policy to protect shared tenants.
amanda: example routing config we might expose to customers (very rough):
```
routing:
  policy: region_affinity
  region_preference: [eu-west-1, us-west-2]
  fallback: shared_pool
  tenant_slice: reserved: 50 # percent of requests routed to reserved pool
```
chris: nice. product/infra also need to agree on guardrails: max reserved % per region, global quotas, and spike-burst handling.
rafael: runtime items: cross-region KV invalidation, prefix cache transfer, and efficient cross-tenant eviction policies. these are blockers for low-latency failover.
sophie: ask PMs to collect specific legal/regulatory constraints per customer (e.g., logs retention in region). will compile.
kevin: prioritization notes: Phase 1 must land before sales can promise anything. Phase 2 can be gated by a set of early-adopter customers paying for reserved capacity. Phase 3 is enterprise-only and needs legal signoff.
amanda: proposed rough timeline: Q2 = Phase 1 (policy API + metrics + flags). Q3 = Phase 2 (tenant slices + reserved capacity + migration tool). Q4 = Phase 3 (hard isolation + compliance).
chris: risk log: 1) cost unpredictability for engineering org, 2) scheduling GPU capacity across markets, 3) complexity in billing and metering.
rafael: mitigation ideas: smart consolidation engine, preemptible burst pool, and per-tenant reclaim policies.
jamal: ops checklist for rollouts:
  - canary to 1% traffic for 24h
  - synthetic regret tests for 72h
  - auto-fallback ON by default
  - billing flags toggled only after explicit purchase
sophie: CS will run an early-adopter beta with two customers and feed acceptance criteria.
kevin: add monitoring SLO: alert if cross-tenant fallback > 0.5% over 10m.
amanda: action items (owners):
  - amanda: product lead & roadmap comms
  - chris: capacity model + guardrails
  - rafael: runtime feasibility + perf targets
  - kevin: dashboard + tracing hooks
  - sophie: customer acceptance + legal requirements collector
  - jamal: rollout runbook & canary tooling
infra-bot: created: roadmap/longterm-routing epic #LR-1423 (staging).
amanda: ok let's sync in architecture sync on Thursday to align WIP and deliverables. please add any missing must-haves before then. :calendar:
